quarterly_data.signal: Q4 FY2026 results (CFO Greg Hebard): revenue approximately $10.6 billion, up 29% year-over-year and more than $1 billion above the midpoint of the June outlook, with the upside driven by Intelligent Infrastructure and Regulated Industries; GAAP operating income $602 million (5.7% of revenue); core operating income $675 million, core operating margin 6.4%; GAAP diluted EPS $3.76; core diluted EPS $4.40, up 34% year-over-year. Revenue and core EPS both exceeded the high end of guidance.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue ~$10.6 billion (+29% YoY); core operating margin 6.4%; core EPS $4.40 (+34%)

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 FY2026 segments (CFO): Intelligent Infrastructure revenue approximately $5.8 billion, up 56% year-over-year and roughly $900 million above the June outlook, because AI-related demand 'remained very strong and continued to accelerate' and capacity came online sooner than planned with customer ramps progressing better than anticipated - supported by the ramp of the second hyperscaler in Mexico, continued strength in networking programs in India and a better-than-expected power business; segment core operating margin 6.5%, up 60 basis points, helped by the margin-accretive Hanley Energy acquisition. 'After being capacity-constrained for much of the year, we are beginning to see our capacity investments drive growth.' Regulated Industries $3.4 billion (+9%, core margin 5.8%; Automotive and Transportation the largest contributor to upside, Healthcare and Packaging lower on automation-equipment delays and a customer program timing shift); Connected Living and Digital Commerce approximately $1.4 billion, roughly flat (core margin 7.1%), renamed Intelligent Devices and Robotics going forward.
quarterly_data.figure: Intelligent Infrastructure ~$5.8 billion (+56% YoY, ~$900 million above outlook), margin 6.5%; Regulated Industries $3.4 billion (+9%); CLDC ~$1.4 billion

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 full year (CEO Mike Dastoor / CFO): revenue grew 21%, core operating margin expanded 40 basis points to 5.8%, core EPS grew 34%, free cash flow expanded by more than $200 million; adjusted free cash flow more than $1.5 billion (above the initial $1.3 billion-plus outlook), cash from operations approximately $2 billion, net capex $470 million or 1.3% of revenue ('we supported $36 billion of revenue on about $470 million of net CapEx'). Gross margin has risen more than 200 basis points since fiscal 2020 to 9.2%; core ROIC has nearly tripled since fiscal 2020 to 59%; approximately 110% of core net earnings converted to cash. Net inventory days fell approximately four days sequentially to 64 (gross approximately 82), still above the 55-60 day target, with management expecting a return to that range through fiscal 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 revenue +21%; core operating margin 5.8%; adjusted FCF >$1.5 billion; net capex $470 million (1.3%); gross margin 9.2%; core ROIC 59%

quarterly_data.signal: FY2027 outlook (CEO): revenue approximately $44.5 billion, up about 24%, adding in excess of $8.5 billion of revenue after more than $6 billion added in fiscal 2026; core operating margin 6.1% (+30 basis points) from revenue growth, better utilization of new capacity and improving mix; core diluted EPS $17.55, up about 34%; adjusted free cash flow approximately $1.6 billion; net capex 1.5%-2% of revenue ('almost closer to the 1.5%'), with Intelligent Infrastructure 'really closer to 1% of revenue' (CFO). Revenue split roughly 45%-55% first half to second half, with margins back-end loaded as roughly 4 million square feet of capacity ramps; CEO: 'we are always appropriately conservative', with possible upside on flawless execution and no major supply-chain issues.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2027 revenue ~$44.5 billion (+24%); core operating margin 6.1%; core EPS $17.55 (+34%); adjusted FCF ~$1.6 billion; net capex 1.5%-2%

quarterly_data.signal: FY2027 segment outlook (CEO): Intelligent Infrastructure approximately $25.6 billion, up about 43% (capital equipment ~$4.2 billion +40%, cloud and data center infrastructure ~$17.5 billion +52%, networking and communications ~$3.9 billion +15%), with six customers in the segment each expected to generate more than $1 billion; Regulated Industries approximately $13.6 billion, up about 7% (Automotive and Transportation ~$5 billion +9% after ~$4.6 billion in fiscal 2026; Healthcare and Packaging ~$5.6 billion +6%; Renewable and Energy Infrastructure ~$3 billion +7%); Intelligent Devices and Robotics approximately $5.3 billion, down about 2% (Digital Commerce and Robotics ~$3 billion +11%; Connected Living ~$2.3 billion -15%, with management 'conservative around memory constraints in this market').
quarterly_data.figure: Intelligent Infrastructure ~$25.6 billion (+43%); Regulated Industries ~$13.6 billion (+7%); IDR ~$5.3 billion (-2%)

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 FY2027 guidance (CFO): revenue $10.6 billion-$11.4 billion; Regulated Industries ~$3.5 billion (+12%), Intelligent Infrastructure ~$6.3 billion (+63%; 'AI hardware-related demand remains very strong and continues to accelerate', supported by customer ramps and additional capacity), Intelligent Devices and Robotics ~$1.2 billion (-10%); GAAP operating income $481 million-$541 million; core operating income $592 million-$652 million; GAAP diluted EPS $2.78-$3.18; core diluted EPS $3.80-$4.20; core tax rate 20%. CEO expects a seasonal dip in Q2 and each quarter to outperform its year-ago comparison.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 revenue $10.6 billion-$11.4 billion; Intelligent Infrastructure ~$6.3 billion (+63%); core EPS $3.80-$4.20

quarterly_data.signal: AI-related revenue (CEO): approximately $14.4 billion in fiscal 2026, up $5.4 billion year-over-year (segment head Matt Crowley: AI-related revenue up 60%), expected to grow to approximately $22.1 billion in fiscal 2027, up 54% - 'a higher growth rate on top of a much larger base, even from our expectations in June'. Jabil ended fiscal 2026 with four customers above $1 billion of annual AI-related revenue (one two years ago) and expects five in fiscal 2027. Matt Crowley: most of the AI business is inference for deployed models at the largest cloud platforms, not frontier training, and 'our direct exposure to frontier model developers is a small fraction of our AI-related revenue'; four of the six largest data center wins this year began as design engagements.
quarterly_data.figure: AI-related revenue ~$14.4 billion FY2026, ~$22.1 billion FY2027 (+54%); four customers >$1 billion, five expected in FY2027

quarterly_data.signal: Hyperscaler customers (CEO / Matt Crowley): the second hyperscaler started with a single capability and has grown into a storage program above $1 billion in annual revenue; its ramp in Mexico is contributing to growth and the CEO expects it to be a 10%+ customer in FY2027. The third hyperscaler, won in the third quarter, is expected to make a modest contribution in fiscal 2027 'with the greater opportunity beyond that'. The largest account grew from a server and rack program into servers, racks, power, cooling and services. Management says the capacity being added is tied to programs already booked: 'We have booked orders. We have customers ready to go.'
quarterly_data.figure: second hyperscaler storage program >$1 billion annual revenue, expected 10%+ customer in FY2027; third hyperscaler modest FY2027 contribution

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and demand (CEO / CFO / Matt Crowley): Jabil is adding about 4 million square feet of capacity, with capacity added this year in Southeast Asia, the U.S., Mexico and India and footprint expansion in Mississippi, Virginia, India, Mexico, Brazil and Vietnam (more than 120 sites in 30 countries, more than 40 in the U.S.). CEO: in Intelligent Infrastructure 'demand is way outweighing supply right now'. Visibility: management feels good about what it sees 12-24 months out and has prepared for an 18-month horizon. Matt Crowley: lower-power data center infrastructure capacity (2 MW-4 MW at 1 million square feet) can be added inside three to four months, while highly complex AI racks requiring 20 MW-30 MW of power for test infrastructure are 'a different profile'. New capacity is mostly in Intelligent Infrastructure; Regulated Industries and warehouse automation use surplus capacity.
quarterly_data.figure: adding ~4 million square feet; 2 MW-4 MW capacity addable in three to four months; complex AI racks need 20 MW-30 MW for test

quarterly_data.signal: Regulation and long-term view: Matt Crowley said Jabil does not see any significant impact or disruption from potential regulation on data center infrastructure for fiscal 2027 and nothing hitting fiscal 2028 so far, though the midterms are a potential inflection point. CEO Mike Dastoor: 'I do not see AI growth slowing down anytime soon. Inference workloads keep expanding'; Jabil exits fiscal 2027 at a meaningfully higher capacity, setting up FY2028; he declined to give FY2028 growth numbers ('Am I saying 2028 will be similar? Maybe.').

Regulated Industries detail (Steve Borges / CEO): the automotive portfolio's electrification and powertrain share was reduced from approximately 80% in fiscal 2023 to about 40% in fiscal 2026, the balance mostly software-defined vehicle, compute and ADAS programs; approximately 90% of fiscal 2026 automotive revenue came directly from OEMs. Defense and Aerospace is expected to be an important growth driver in fiscal 2027 as new programs move into production. In drug delivery Jabil expects to manufacture more than 700 million injectors and delivery pens in fiscal 2027; new auto-injector wins require expansion of the North Carolina site; the Croatia facility ramp continues in fiscal 2027 with full production in fiscal 2028. Renewable and Energy Infrastructure is broadening into energy storage, electrical infrastructure, data center cooling and commercial power, with targeted inorganic growth in power electronics and low-voltage switchgear.
quarterly_data.figure: auto electrification share ~80% (FY2023) to ~40% (FY2026); >700 million injectors and pens in FY2027

quarterly_data.signal: Intelligent Devices and Robotics (Rafael Renno / CEO): the renamed segment shifts from consumer products toward robotics and automation (ASRS warehouse systems, mobile robots, retail technology, autonomous last-mile delivery) and engages early with humanoid robot developers on actuators and robotic hands. A Symbotic procurement executive said in the presentation that Jabil has scaled Symbotic's bot production since 2023, reaching 10,000 bots in June 2025 and approaching 20,000 in total. CEO: physical AI is at a very early commercialization stage with negligible real-world deployment in the West; the FY2027 forecast for physical AI is 'modest and conservative', and he expects substantial growth in the mid to longer term ('is this a 2028 event? Is it a 2029? Only time will tell').
quarterly_data.figure: Symbotic bots: 10,000 in June 2025, approaching 20,000 in total

players.product: Contract-manufactured server/GPU PCBs with MLCC population

quarterly_data.signal: Supply constraints (Chief Supply Chain Officer Frank McKay): 'We are seeing real constraints today. Memory, in particular, is being reallocated towards AI and hyperscale demand, tightening supply across many of the diversified end markets that we serve' - which management views as 'a structural shift in global capacity', compounded by geopolitical disruption. Jabil engages about 120 strategic suppliers like customers ('allocation follows trust as much as order size'); in cloud and data center infrastructure large customers play a key role in securing supply. McKay: 'I wouldn't suggest that we are immune', expecting 'some bumps' through fiscal 2027 but confident in the supply structure; access to supply in 'a very constrained marketplace' is what keeps him up at night. Jabil manages approximately $35 billion of global spend across 40,000 suppliers (CEO). Higher commodity pricing and a heavier inventory weighting in cloud data center infrastructure contributed to inventory levels (CFO).
quarterly_data.figure: about 120 strategic suppliers; ~$35 billion global spend; 40,000 suppliers

quarterly_data.signal: Capital equipment (Matt Crowley / CEO): revenue grew about 20% in fiscal 2026 and is expected at approximately $4.2 billion in fiscal 2027, up approximately 40%, as automated test equipment demand stays strong with more complex silicon and memory and the wafer fab equipment market inflects higher. Jabil brought a new site in Vietnam into production and is building complete subsystems for a new generation of memory testers using thermal control developed in its data center work, moving from components into modules and subsystems.

players.product: Silicon photonics / co-packaged optics manufacturing + system integration (ex-Intel photonics business)

quarterly_data.signal: Networking (CFO Greg Hebard / CEO): networking and communications is expected at approximately $3.9 billion in fiscal 2027, up approximately 15%, but the networking business itself is growing roughly 45%-50% - the reported line is held down by weakness in communications/5G ('bouncing around the bottom'). Advanced AI networking programs in India are a major contributor; Matt Crowley: when a switch customer needed capacity for a new generation of AI switches, Jabil brought India production online at record pace, and those lines now build liquid-cooled network racks.
quarterly_data.figure: networking and communications ~$3.9 billion (+15%) FY2027; networking growth roughly 45%-50%

quarterly_data.signal: Silicon photonics and co-packaged optics (Matt Crowley / CEO): Jabil's photonics team supplies the silicon photonics transceivers that connect the liquid-cooled AI network racks it builds in India, and 'co-packaged optics move the optics onto the switch silicon'. CEO: the 2023 Intel acquisition plus investments in high-speed interconnects and optics 'position us well to support co-packaged optics and co-packaged copper technologies as they start to scale'; he is 'excited about the opportunity that co-packaged optics proliferation presents for us in networking'.

players.product: Data-center power + thermal manufacturing (LV/MV switchgear, in-row heat exchangers, modular power distribution via Hanley) and next-gen liquid-cooled AI rack integration

quarterly_data.signal: Data center power and cooling (Matt Crowley / CEO): Jabil is building modular data centers - power and cooling modules built and tested in the factory - in Guadalajara and Salt Lake City so customers reach power months sooner; Hanley Energy adds power engineering, deployment and services, and that services capability is 'the highest margin business in the segment'. Jabil brings its own technology where it fills a gap, in cold plates, chillers and power distribution, but positions itself as integrating customers' chosen platforms rather than standardizing them on its own power and cooling products. The power business beat expectations in Q4 FY2026. CEO cites Mikros Technologies (liquid cooling) and Hanley Energy (data center power) as acquisition models, and remains 'extremely bullish on the India data center build-out' through the strategic alliance with the Adani Group.
